models.name: todo_list_configurations
models.description:
System-wide configuration settings and feature flags governing application behavior and operational parameters.

Stores key-value pairs that control application features, operational parameters, and behavioral settings across the entire system. These configurations are managed by administrators through administrative interfaces and affect system-wide behavior rather than individual user experience.

Configuration values can control feature toggles, rate limits, timeouts, external service endpoints, and other operational settings. The enabled flag allows administrators to activate or deactivate configurations without deleting them, maintaining audit trails for compliance.

This table is referenced by various system components to determine their runtime behavior based on centralized configuration.

plainFields.name: configuration_key
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for the configuration setting (e.g., "feature_toggles.new_ui", "api.rate_limit.per_minute"). Must be unique across all configurations.

plainFields.name: configuration_value
plainFields.description: The actual value of the configuration setting. Can represent boolean ("true"/"false"), numbers, strings, JSON objects, or any other data format. Stored as string to accommodate any configuration type.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation of what this configuration controls, its expected values, and its impact on system behavior. Used by administrators to understand configuration purpose.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Whether this configuration is active and affecting system behavior. When false, the system should ignore this configuration regardless of its value.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was created. Used for audit trail and debugging purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was last modified. Updated automatically on any change to the configuration.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was logically deleted. Used for soft deletion to maintain audit trails while allowing configurations to be deactivated without permanent deletion.

models.name: todo_list_tokens
models.description:
Authentication tokens (access and refresh) issued to users, tracking validity, expiration, and revocation status.

Manages the lifecycle of tokens associated with authenticated sessions. Each token is linked to exactly one session (user, admin, or guest) and contains either an access token or refresh token value.

Access tokens are short-lived and used for API authentication, while refresh tokens are longer-lived and used to obtain new access tokens when expired. The system tracks token expiration and revocation to enforce secure authentication policies.

Tokens are automatically revoked when users log out or when sessions expire. The revoked_at field allows for explicit revocation before expiration and supports audit trails of security incidents.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_session_id
foreignFields.description: Session that issued this token. {@link todo_list_user_sessions.id}.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_admin_session_id
foreignFields.description: Session that issued this token. {@link todo_list_admin_sessions.id}.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_guest_session_id
foreignFields.description: Session that issued this token. {@link todo_list_guest_sessions.id}.

plainFields.name: token_type
plainFields.description: Type of authentication token: 'access' for short-lived API tokens, 'refresh' for long-lived token renewal tokens. Cannot be null - every token must be explicitly classified.

plainFields.name: token_value
plainFields.description: The actual cryptographic token value issued for authentication. Must be a secure, random string that cannot be guessed. Used to authenticate API requests.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: The exact timestamp when the token expires and becomes invalid. This is a required security field - sessions cannot grant unlimited access. All tokens must have an expiration time.

plainFields.name: revoked_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the token was explicitly revoked before expiration. NULL means token has not been voluntarily revoked. Used for audit trails when users log out or security events occur.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this token was originally issued and stored in the database.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this token was last modified (typically updated when revoked).

models.name: todo_list_logs
models.description:
Audit logs for critical system operations such as authentication events, configuration changes, and security alerts.

Tracks all significant system events for security monitoring, compliance auditing, and system troubleshooting. Each log entry records the actor responsible, the type of event, contextual metadata, and connection details.

Log entries are append-only and never modified after creation. The system uses these logs to reconstruct the sequence of operations for forensic analysis and to enforce security policies.

Soft deletion is supported to maintain data integrity during regulatory compliance requirements while allowing administrative cleanup of obsolete records.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: User who triggered the event. {@link todo_list_user.id}.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Guest session that triggered the event. {@link todo_list_guest.id}.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who triggered the event. {@link todo_list_admin.id}.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_session_id
foreignFields.description: User session context for the event. {@link todo_list_user_sessions.id}.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_guest_session_id
foreignFields.description: Guest session context for the event. {@link todo_list_guest_sessions.id}.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_admin_session_id
foreignFields.description: Admin session context for the event. {@link todo_list_admin_sessions.id}.

plainFields.name: event_category
plainFields.description: High-level category of the event. Values: 'authentication', 'configuration', 'security', 'system', 'request'.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Specific event that occurred. Examples: 'login', 'logout', 'password_change', 'config_update', 'failed_login', 'access_denied'.

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: JSON string containing additional context about the event (e.g., changed fields, error codes, request parameters).

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address from which the request originated.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string identifying the client application/browser.

plainFields.name: session_id
plainFields.description: Session identifier associated with this event (unique identifier for the session, not the ID field).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the log entry was created. The time at which the event occurred.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the log entry was last updated. Always equal to created_at as logs are immutable.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the log entry was logically deleted by an administrator. Used for compliance cleanup. Event data remains intact for audit.

models.name: todo_list_rate_limits
models.description:
System-wide rate limit enforcement for protecting infrastructure from abuse.

Tracks request quotas per client IP address or authenticated user to prevent rate flooding and denial-of-service attacks. Each record represents a specific limitation configuration that expires after a time window, ensuring stateful counting with automatic cleanup.

Rate limits can be applied by IP address or linked to authentication by user ID. The system automatically invalidates expired limits during cleanup operations and allows administrators to reset limits manually for debugging or user support.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: The authenticated user whose requests are being rate limited. {@link todo_list_user.id}.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: Client IP address that generated the requests. Used as primary limiting identifier for unauthenticated clients.

plainFields.name: request_count
plainFields.description: Number of requests counted within the current time window. Resets to zero upon expiration.

plainFields.name: window_seconds
plainFields.description: Duration of the rate limiting window in seconds (e.g., 60 for 1-minute window).

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this rate limit expires and should be reset. Used for automated cleanup of old limits.

plainFields.name: limit_type
plainFields.description: Type of rate limit: 'ip' for IP-based limits, 'user' for authenticated user limits.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this rate limit record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this rate limit record was last updated (request count incremented).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for audit trails. When set, the limit is considered inactive but retained for historical analysis.

models.name: todo_list_health_checks
models.description:
Tracks the health status of core system dependencies to ensure 99.9% availability.

Captures point-in-time measurements of critical system components including database connectivity, cache performance, and external service availability. Records timestamps for all health checks to build an audit trail of system reliability over time.

This table follows an append-only pattern where previous health states are preserved for historical analysis and incident investigation. New records are added periodically by system monitoring processes, and records are never updated in place. Soft delete is supported to maintain the integrity of historical audit trails while allowing for data moderation policies.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current health status of the monitored component. Valid values: 'healthy', 'degraded', 'unavailable'. Indicates the operational state of the system dependency at the time of check.

plainFields.name: latency
plainFields.description: Response latency in milliseconds observed during the health check. Null indicates no latency measurement was performed or available for this check.

plainFields.name: error_message
plainFields.description: Detailed error message describing the failure condition when status is 'degraded' or 'unavailable'. Null when status is 'healthy' or when no error occurred.

plainFields.name: database_uptime
plainFields.description: Database service uptime percentage during the health check. Value between 0 and 100. Null when database health check not performed.

plainFields.name: cache_response_time
plainFields.description: Average cache response time in milliseconds during the health check. Null when cache service not monitored.

plainFields.name: external_service_one_status
plainFields.description: Status of first external service dependency. Valid values: 'healthy', 'degraded', 'unavailable'. Null when not monitored.

plainFields.name: external_service_two_status
plainFields.description: Status of second external service dependency. Valid values: 'healthy', 'degraded', 'unavailable'. Null when not monitored.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the health check record was created. Represents the exact moment the system state was measured.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the health check record was last updated. In this model, this will typically equal created_at as records are never modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating when this health check record was logically deleted. Maintained for audit trail purposes and data governance compliance.

models.name: todo_list_versions
models.description:
Tracks historical versions of application code, database schema, and deployment configurations to ensure infrastructure consistency and enable rollback capabilities.

Records exact state snapshots of system components at time of deployment, creating an immutable audit trail of system evolution. Each version record captures the specific code version, schema version, deployment environment, and changelog notes for full traceability.

Used for rollback procedures, deployment verification, and infrastructure change analysis. This is an append-only historical record that should never be modified after creation.

plainFields.name: version
plainFields.description: Application code version identifier following semantic versioning format (e.g., '1.2.3'). Uniquely identifies each deployment state.

plainFields.name: schema_version
plainFields.description: Database schema version identifier following semantic versioning format (e.g., '2.1.0'). Tracks exact state of database structure at time of deployment.

plainFields.name: deployed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this version was deployed in the target environment. Records exact point-in-time of the deployment action.

plainFields.name: environment
plainFields.description: Deployment environment identifier. Valid values: development, staging, production. Specifies the target system for this version deployment.

plainFields.name: changelog
plainFields.description: Detailed changelog describing changes included in this version. Contains human-readable summary of code, schema, and configuration modifications.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this version record was created in the database. Automatically set to match deployment time for audit consistency.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this version record was last updated. Always equals created_at since snapshot tables are immutable.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null indicates record is active. Used for system-level data retention policies while maintaining audit trail integrity.

models.name: todo_list_user
models.description:
Authenticated user account with email, password hash, and profile information.

Represents the primary identity record for users who can log in to the system and manage personal todo lists.

Each user has a unique email address for authentication, and their password is stored as a hashed value for security. The table maintains a soft delete capability to preserve audit trails while allowing account deactivation.

This actor entity has a one-to-many relationship with todo_list_user_sessions, which tracks all login sessions for the user.

User accounts are created through registration workflow and are never shared between users.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: User's unique email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all users.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for authentication. Never stored in plain text. Generated using strong hashing algorithm with salt.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was soft-deleted. Null indicates account is active.

models.name: todo_list_guest
models.description:
Represents unauthenticated visitors with no account data - used only for system state tracking.

This actor type enables the system to track and maintain state for anonymous users who interact with public content. Unlike authenticated users, guest actors don't have login credentials or persistent profiles, but still require a unique identifier and session tracking to maintain temporary state across HTTP requests.

The guest entity provides a consistent actor pattern across all user types in the system, allowing unified authentication flows and session management even for anonymous access. Guest records are temporary and typically persist only for the duration of a browsing session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this guest actor record was created. Mandatory for tracking session lifecycle.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this guest actor record was last updated. Used for session activity tracking.

models.name: todo_list_admin
models.description:
Stores administrative user accounts with elevated system access privileges.

Represents the canonical identity record for administrative users who require elevated permissions and system access. Each admin account contains authentication credentials and profile data necessary for secure system administration.

This table is the source of truth for admin authentication and is referenced by admin_sessions table for session tracking. It separates administrative identity management from other user types following domain separation principles. Admins have unrestricted access to system functions and are responsible for maintaining system security and user management.

All admin accounts are subject to audit logging and strict credential requirements. Soft deletion is supported to maintain audit trails while allowing administrative account deactivation.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique admin email address for authentication and system notifications.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed password for authentication. Never store plain text passwords.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last profile update or password change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin account was soft-deleted (null means active).

models.name: todo_list_user_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for authenticated todo_list_user accounts, tracking login state, connection context, and session expiration.

Each session represents a single authenticated login event from a user. The table captures essential connection details (IP address, request URL, referrer) and enforces session lifetime through mandatory expiration.

Sessions are append-only - never updated or soft-deleted. Instead, expired sessions are purged by system maintenance. Primary purpose is security: limiting concurrent sessions and detecting suspicious access patterns.

The user_id foreign key references todo_list_user.id, establishing ownership. Any new login creates a new session record, preserving historical access patterns for auditing.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: The authenticated user this session belongs to. {@link todo_list_user.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The full URL requested when this session was created.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The website or application that referred the user to this system.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created (first login event).

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expires and becomes invalid. Sessions must expire for security - unlimited sessions are prohibited.

models.name: todo_list_admin_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for todo_list_admin, tracking tokens and login states.

Tracks active and expired login sessions for administrative users of the system. Each session records the connection context (IP address, URL, referrer) and timestamps for session lifecycle management.

Session records are append-only for audit trail purposes and do not represent user identity information (which resides in the todo_list_admin table). When a session expires, its expired_at field is set to the timestamp of expiration, after which it is no longer considered valid for authentication purposes.

Sessions are automatically created during login and terminated during logout or automatically after a system-defined timeout period.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address from which the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL (path and query parameters) that initiated the session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL indicating the source that redirected the user to the system.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created and validated.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expired. Sessions must expire for security reasons. Non-null by default.

models.name: todo_list_guest_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for todo_list_guest, tracking anonymous access state and temporary tokens.

Tracks the connection context and temporal state of unauthenticated guest visitors interacting with the system. Each session represents a temporary access period during which a guest may view public content or maintain transient preferences.

Sessions are created when a guest first interacts with the system and expire after a defined period of inactivity or system-defined duration. Sessions are append-only and not updated once created. Deleted sessions are logically removed through expiration rather than hard deletion.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the guest user's {@link todo_list_guest.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address from which the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The URL that was accessed during this session connection.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The referrer URL that prompted the guest's access to this system.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest session will expire. Sessions must expire for security - unlimited sessions are not permitted.

models.name: todo_list_todos
models.description:
Individual todo items owned by authenticated users with title, completion status, and timestamps.

Each todo item represents a discrete task that a user creates, manages, and completes within their personal todo list. Todo items are intrinsically linked to the user who created them through a foreign key relationship, ensuring complete data isolation between users.

Items support full lifecycle management: creation with title, toggling completion status, and deletion. All modifications are tracked with precise timestamps. Soft deletion is implemented to maintain audit trails while allowing user-initiated removal.

This table is fundamental to the Todo component's core functionality, providing persistent storage for user-specific task data without duplicating user authentication information.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: The user who owns this todo item. {@link todo_list_user.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Title of the todo item (1-500 characters). The primary identifier for the task that users enter and manage.

plainFields.name: completed
plainFields.description: Completion status of the todo item. True indicates the task is marked complete, false indicates it is still pending.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this todo item was created. Always set to current time on creation and never modified afterwards.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this todo item was last modified. Updated on any change to title or completion status.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this todo item was soft-deleted by the user. NULL indicates the item is still active. Used to support undelete functionality and audit trails.
